title: Dockyard oncall pocket diary - Damian - 2028-07-15
content:
Quick notes from midnight->dawn shift. Pocket diary style, mostly stuff for me to pick up tomorrow. Not a formal postmortem — just the things I need to remember and the small runbook edits I want to make.

00:12 - page: high error rate on hosted-api-us-west-2 (INC-2198)
  - initial triage: upstream GRPC pool exhausted on inference-router-3
  - symptoms: 502 spikes, client retries, latency jump from 45ms -> 220ms p50
  - triage commands:
      kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference-router -o wide
      kubectl logs inference-router-3 -c router --since=15m | grep -i "connection reset"
  - immediate mitigation: scaled inference-router replica from 3 -> 6 (manual) at 00:25
  - short-term help: enabled fallback-route to model-compat-2 (lower throughput but healthy) at 00:31
  - impact: traffic rerouted for ~6 mins; error rate dropped to baseline by 00:38
  - follow-ups: why did the connection pool exhaust? suspect ephemeral gRPC connection leak in libpool v1.12.

00:45 - observations/metrics
  - router CPU on node type g5.x4 spiked to 92% on inference-router-3 before restart
  - KV cache hit ratio dipped ~7% during the spike (we saw more cold starts)
  - small cohort of customers saw degraded throughput (ticketed by CS: CS-2107)

01:10 - temporary runbook note (to formalize later)
  - add a step to router runbook: "If GRPC pool exhaustion suspected, check connection count and recycle router pod; scale up before full recycle if p95 latency > 200ms"
  - add command snippets and thresholds (p95 > 180ms OR 5xx rate > 1% for 3m)

01:35 - post-incident quick hits
  - open follow-ups: INC-2198 assigned to @mira. Needs stacktrace correlation between router and libpool.
  - engineering action: roll forward libpool patch (PR: github.com/redwood/libpool/pulls/142) to a canary cluster 08:00 PT tomorrow.
  - observability: missing span context in router->backend calls; need to ensure trace IDs survive the connection reuse path. Add traces to SLO dashboard.

02:00 - small feature request from CS during the incident:
  - allow customers to opt into "aggressive-fallback" route when tail latency spikes. Noting here: product/CS sync required.

Runbook TODOs (my personal checklist)
  - [ ] Add explicit pool-leak troubleshooting steps to inference-router runbook (priority: high)
  - [ ] Add automated alert: "router grpc connections > 1500 for > 5m" -> page oncall + run escalation to scale policy
  - [ ] Patch runbook snippet with kubectl commands + grep patterns used tonight
  - [ ] Create SLO dashboard tile correlating router connection counts with KV cache hit ratio
  - [ ] Draft short note for CS about how fallback routing behaves (for customer-facing explanations)

Notes for tomorrow (tickets and times)
  - 08:00 - deploy libpool patch to canary cluster (follow PR checklist) -> @leo will verify smoke tests
  - 10:00 - sync with product/CS re: aggressive-fallback opt-in (calendar invite: tentative)
  - 14:00 - runbook grooming session (30m) to merge changes; include Mira and Sam from infra

Unresolved questions / things to investigate
  - Does the connection leak correlate with a specific client pattern? Look at top N client IPs for 1 hour before spike. (INC-2198 logs + access-proxy traces)
  - Why did KV cache hit ratio drop? Hypothesis: increased cold-starts due to pod recycling and scaled-up clients hitting new instances without warmed cache. Validate by checking cache load patterns by pod.
  - Are we underprovisioned for night-boundary traffic (00:00-01:00)? Check historical weekly patterns. If yes, consider small auto-scale policy bump for midnight window.

Personal reminders (less formal)
  - Eat something before next shift. Long night drains me.
  - Push the canary PR; set it to "don’t auto merge" until smoke verified.
  - Remember to include trace-id example in runbook so SRE oncall can paste it in Slack when asking infra/rt for help.

Anything to copy into a formal postmortem?
  - Yes: incident timeline, root-cause hypothesis (libpool leak), mitigation steps and duration, suggested permanent remediations (patch + pool metrics + alerting). I'll hand this to Mira to draft.

Snippets to paste into later formal doc:
  - "Mitigation: scaled inference-router from 3->6 and enabled model fallback; error rate normalized in ~13 minutes"
  - "Suspected root cause: connection pool leak in libpool v1.12 causing connection exhaustion; reproduce locally with high-concurrency client harness"

Quick list of commands I used (for runbook copy/paste)
  - kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference-router -o wide
  - kubectl top pod inference-router-3 --containers
  - kubectl logs inference-router-3 -c router --since=30m | egrep "error|connection|reset|leak" -i
  - curl -sS http://observability.internal/api/metrics?query=router_conn_count | jq

End of night scribbles. Will tidy into a proper runbook PR tomorrow.

-- Damian
  (oncall: dockyard night shift)
